h1: Hull Gauging in Algeciras: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement at Berth and Anchor
intro: Algeciras sits on one of the world's busiest shipping lanes: mainline container ships relaying cargo, tankers serving the refinery at San Roque, ro-pax ferries shuttling to Tanger Med and Ceuta, and a steady queue of ships taking bunkers in the bay. When a superintendent needs thickness gauging in Algeciras between calls, we mobilise a team from India, plan the work around the ship's berth window or anchorage stay, and deliver readings laid out the way the attending surveyor will review them.

highlights.p: Ships in Algeciras are usually here for a relay call, a bunkering stop or a refinery berth. We scope the gauging to the hours actually available and agree priorities with the superintendent before anyone boards.
One mobilisation can cover Algeciras berths, the bay's anchorages and the drydocks at Gibraltar and in the Bay of Cádiz, so measurements started afloat can be completed when the ship docks.

Mediterranean ECA compliance keeps scrubbers running in the bay. We gauge wash-water, overboard and sea-water lines and the shell connections they serve, reporting wall loss against nominal thickness and earlier readings.

port.h: Algeciras Bay: transhipment, bunkering and the Strait trades
p: Algeciras is one of the main container transhipment hubs of the Mediterranean. Its terminals relay boxes between Asia–Europe, transatlantic and West Africa services, so the quays handle the largest container ships in service alongside the feeders that redistribute cargo around the western Mediterranean and the Iberian Atlantic coast. Car carriers and general cargo ships also work the port, though containers dominate the quay line. The Autoridad Portuaria de la Bahía de Algeciras also runs the port of Tarifa, and between the two the ro-pax links to Tanger Med, Tangier and Ceuta operate all year, with the heaviest traffic during the summer Operación Paso del Estrecho.

The bay is equally a liquid-bulk and bunkering anchorage. Crude and product tankers serve the refinery at San Roque, and ships transiting the Strait regularly divert into the bay simply to take fuel from barges at anchor before continuing into the Mediterranean or out into the Atlantic. Bulk carriers, tankers and car carriers waiting for orders, a berth or a crew change add to the anchorage population. Many of these ships are present for hours rather than days, and planning gauging around that window is what separates inspection work here from work at a repair port.

Algeciras is not primarily a drydock port, so gauging here is nearly always done afloat: at a container berth during a long relay call, at a tanker berth, or at anchor during bunkering or a wait for orders. The work that fits is targeted — confirming suspect areas reported by the crew, measuring scrubber wash-water piping, checking fire main and ballast lines after a port state control remark, or taking pre-docking readings in ballast tanks so the yard has a steel renewal estimate in hand when the ship arrives. Full renewal-survey gauging on a large tanker or bulk carrier is better programmed into the docking itself, and the nearest drydocks are across the bay at Gibraltar and along the coast in the Bay of Cádiz.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens around Algeciras Bay
p: Gauging in Algeciras is planned around one of three settings: a terminal berth, a liquid-bulk berth or the anchorage. On a container ship, the terminal's crane programme and lashing gangs set the pace, so the team works in spaces that do not interfere with cargo — engine-room and double-bottom tanks, void spaces, the steering gear flat and the scrubber casing. At tanker berths, permit-to-work and gas-free rules decide what can be entered: cargo tanks are gauged only when the ship is gas-free, while deck structure, pump rooms and segregated ballast tanks are usually accessible once the permits are in place.

At anchor, the limits are launch access, the weather in the Strait and how long the ship will stay. A strong Levante, the easterly wind funnelled through the Strait, can make boarding from a launch difficult or suspend it altogether, so anchorage jobs need some float in the plan. The ultrasonic gauges and magnetic particle kit travel with the technicians and go aboard by launch, so no shore equipment is needed. When the scope grows to a full survey programme, combining afloat work in Algeciras with the remaining measurements at a nearby drydock usually makes the best use of the ship's time.

context.h: Port state control, the Med ECA and transhipment economics
p: Spain is a Paris MoU state, and port state control inspections in Algeciras are carried out by inspectors of the Capitanía Marítima, the harbour-master authority of the Spanish maritime administration. Structural corrosion found during an inspection — wasted deck plating, holed air pipes or a thinned fire main — can lead to a detention, and owners then need gauging at short notice so that class and the flag can decide on repairs. Since 1 May 2025 the bay has been inside the Mediterranean SOx ECA established under MARPOL Annex VI regulation 14: ships without scrubbers burn 0.10% sulphur fuel, while scrubber-equipped ships keep their systems running, and their wash-water piping keeps corroding.

Commercially, Algeciras competes with Tanger Med across the Strait for the same transhipment business. With EU ETS covering shipping since 2024 and FuelEU Maritime since 2025, carriers now weigh emissions exposure as well as port time when they plan relays, and the outcome decides how long their ships spend in the bay. For technical managers this has a practical effect: a mainline vessel's Algeciras call is usually tight, but feeders, ships waiting for a slot and vessels laid by between rotations can offer a usable window for inspection, provided the gauging plan is ready before the ship arrives.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Algeciras
jobs.p: Gauging in Algeciras is usually scoped tightly, because the ship's time in port is set by cargo or bunkering rather than by the inspection. The jobs below are the kind of work that fits a berth or anchorage window here; anything larger is planned into a docking, with Algeciras used to gather data beforehand. We agree the measurement plan with the superintendent before the team travels, so the time on board is spent measuring rather than locating spaces.
list: Scrubber pipe inspection on a container ship during a relay call: ultrasonic gauging of wash-water and overboard lines plus the shell connection area, with readings mapped against the previous survey.
Ballast tank readings on a Capesize bulk carrier at anchor during bunkering, with its third renewal survey coming up, giving the chosen yard a steel renewal estimate in advance of the docking.
Pre-purchase thickness gauging at anchor on a product tanker changing hands, sampling deck, bottom and ballast tank structure to give the buyer a corrosion picture before the delivery decision.
Magnetic particle crack detection at stern ramp hinges and car-deck supporting structure on a Strait ro-pax ferry during an off-season maintenance period, with gauging of the surrounding plating.
Fire main and sea-water piping gauging on a tanker alongside at San Roque after a port state control remark on corroded piping, giving class measured wall thickness to decide on repairs.

logistics: For Algeciras, the usual routing from India is into Málaga, Seville or Jerez through a European or Gulf hub, then by road to the bay; Gibraltar's airport is another option when UK connections suit. Terminal and jetty access goes through the ship's agent, who requests ISPS gate passes and lists the technicians for the terminal. For anchorage jobs the agent also secures a launch, timed so the technicians board as the ship starts bunkering or settles to wait. Technicians travel on Schengen visas, so the earlier we know the expected call, the more reliably the mobilisation can be fixed.

faqs.q: Is a bunkering stop in Algeciras Bay long enough for gauging?
faqs.a: For targeted work, often yes. A bunkering stop leaves time for scrubber piping, a suspect ballast tank, a deck area flagged by the crew, or sample readings for a buyer. A full renewal-survey scope will not fit. If you share the expected anchoring time and the list of spaces, we will tell you plainly whether the window is realistic.

faqs.q: Does the Mediterranean ECA apply in Algeciras?
faqs.a: Yes. The ECA is bounded to the west by a meridian inside the Strait, near Tarifa, and Algeciras Bay lies east of that line, so the Mediterranean SOx limits have applied there since 1 May 2025. Scrubber-equipped ships calling at Algeciras run their systems throughout the stay, which leaves the wash-water and overboard lines exposed to acidic water for the whole call and makes periodic ultrasonic gauging of them worthwhile.

faqs.q: Where should a ship dock if the Algeciras gauging shows substantial corrosion?
faqs.a: That decision belongs to the owner and class, but the nearest drydocks are at Gibraltar and in the Bay of Cádiz, with further yards along the Spanish Mediterranean coast. Gauging at Algeciras before the docking gives the chosen yard a steel list to plan against, and the same technicians can travel on to the yard to take the remaining measurements once the ship is dry.

faqs.q: How are gauging results handled when port state control raises a corrosion deficiency in Algeciras?
faqs.a: We measure the affected structure or piping, record the readings against original thickness and the allowable diminution, and report so that the class surveyor and the flag can decide on repairs or a condition of class. Whether readings are credited for class purposes depends on that society's rules for thickness measurement firms, so we confirm the arrangement with your class contact before work starts.
